title: Bridging the Gap Between Anchor-based and Anchor-free Detection via Adaptive Training Sample Selection

problem.summary: The paper says the reported advantage of anchor-free detectors (e.g. FCOS over RetinaNet) is confounded by implementation differences, and that once those are removed the real gap comes from how positive and negative training samples are defined, a choice made with fragile hand-set hyperparameters (IoU thresholds, scale ranges).
statements: The claimed performance gap between anchor-based and anchor-free detectors mixes universal improvements (GroupNorm, GIoU, centerness, in-box sampling) with the essential difference of positive/negative sample definition.
Traditional sample-selection strategies depend on sensitive hyperparameters such as IoU thresholds and per-level scale ranges, so some objects are neglected under fixed rules.
Tiling multiple anchors per location is claimed to be useful, but its actual role is unclear under better sample selection.

evidence.quote: the essential difference between anchor-based and anchor-free detection is actually how to define positive and negative training samples, which leads to the performance gap between them.
However, as reported in [56], FCOS outperforms RetinaNet (#A=1) by a large margin in AP performance on the MS COCO minival subset, i.e., 37.1% vs. 32.5%.
Previous sample selection strategies have some sensitive hyperparameters, such as IoU thresholds in anchor-based detectors and scale ranges in anchor-free detectors.
We argue that tiling multiple anchors per location is a useless operation under our proposed method and it needs further study to discover its right role.

background.summary: The study builds on the anchor-based lineage (Faster R-CNN, SSD, RetinaNet) and the anchor-free lineage (keypoint-based CornerNet/ExtremeNet/CenterNet and center-based FCOS/FoveaBox), comparing RetinaNet and FCOS in a controlled setting to isolate sample definition from regression starting point.

solution.summary: Adaptive Training Sample Selection (ATSS) assigns positives per ground-truth box by taking the k closest-centre anchors from every pyramid level, computing the mean and standard deviation of their IoUs, and labelling candidates above t_g = m_g + v_g (and whose centre lies inside the object) as positives; the paper also shows that with such selection the number of anchors per location no longer matters.
solution.approach: Select positives per ground-truth from the k nearest anchors on each pyramid level using an adaptive IoU threshold equal to the mean plus standard deviation of the candidate IoUs, with candidate centres constrained inside the object.
components: candidate positives: k anchors per pyramid level closest to the ground-truth centre by L2 distance (k x L candidates)
adaptive per-object IoU threshold t_g = mean(IoU) + std(IoU) of the candidates
centre-in-ground-truth constraint that removes poor candidates
conflict rule: an anchor assigned to several ground-truths goes to the highest-IoU one
single hyperparameter k (default 9), making the method nearly hyperparameter-free
shared application to anchor-based RetinaNet and anchor-free FCOS (plus a centre-sampling lite variant)

evidence.quote: we propose an Adaptive Training Sample Selection (ATSS) to automatically select positive and negative samples according to statistical characteristics of object
on each pyramid level, we select k anchor boxes whose center are closest to the center of g based on L2 distance.
Finally, we select these candidates whose IoU are greater than or equal to the threshold tg as final positive samples
if an anchor box is assigned to multiple ground-truth boxes, the one with the highest IoU will be selected.
Our method only has one hyperparameter k. Subsequent experiments prove that it is quite insensitive to the variations of k and the proposed ATSS can be considered almost hyperparameter-free.

experiments.summary: Experiments use MS COCO with 115K trainval35k images for training and 5K minival for analysis, first reproducing a controlled RetinaNet-vs-FCOS comparison, then verifying ATSS on both detectors, ablating k, anchor scale/aspect ratio and the number of anchors per location, and finally reporting test-dev results with multi-scale training and testing.

benchmarks.split: test-dev, ATSS (ResNet-101), no bells and whistles

evidence.quote: our method with ResNet-101 achieves 43.6% AP without any bells and whistles
The best result 47.7% is achieved with singlemodel and single-scale testing, outperforming all the previous detectors by a large margin.
Finally, with the multiscale testing strategy, our best model achieves 50.7% AP.
it consistently boosts the performance by 2.3% on AP

limitations.summary: The authors note that the lite centre-sampling variant still carries FCOS's fixed scale-range hyperparameters, that very small k hurts accuracy through statistical instability, and that the role of multiple anchors per location still needs study; the analysis is also built on RetinaNet/FCOS comparisons.
items: The lite version (center sampling) keeps the scale-range hyperparameters of FCOS, so it is not hyperparameter-free.
Too small k (e.g. 3) gives too few candidates and statistical instability, causing a noticeable accuracy drop.
The claim that multiple anchors per location are unnecessary is argued for the current setup and left open for further study.
Analysis is centred on a ResNet-50 RetinaNet/FCOS comparison on COCO.

evidence.quote: the hyperparameters of scale ranges still exist in the lite version.
Too small k (e.g., 3) causes a noticeable drop in accuracy, because too few candidate positive samples will cause statistical instability.
We argue that tiling multiple anchors per location is a useless operation under our proposed method and it needs further study to discover its right role.

futureDirections.direction: Re-examine what role tiling multiple anchors per location actually plays once positives are selected adaptively.

applications.detail: ATSS only redefines positive/negative samples, so it adds no inference cost and can be plugged into existing detectors.
applications.quote: Since our method only redefines positive and negative samples without incurring any additional overhead, these improvements can be considered cost-free.
